summary: 1923 wood ground cab on Cone Peak, later sheathed in metal and full of radio gear; the Forest Service lists the site closed after the 2026 fires.

facts.design: Ground cab on a rock foundation: a 13 by 13 foot wooden cab, later clad in metal siding, with a flat roof from 1959
facts.status_note: Still standing, but the cab holds radio repeater equipment and is not in use as a lookout.

access.note: Forest Service listing, updated August 31, 2026: site closed after the Timber and Plaskett Fires; emergency closure order with exceptions applies

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 'all-metal tower' comes from the 2020 FFLA California-South report. The register and the Forest Lookouts page describe a wooden 13 by 13 foot ground cab on a rock foundation that was later sided in metal. The story reports both descriptions.

notes_for_editor: The Forest Service page (updated August 31, 2026) lists the site as closed after the Timber and Plaskett Fires and says it is reachable only on foot; the story says so and does not encourage a visit. The record's 'all-metal tower' design conflicts with the register and Forest Lookouts descriptions of a wooden ground cab later sided in metal; it is kept in facts.design and the record's design field is not on the corrections list, so please decide whether to change it. status stays 'standing' in the record; the status_note is a judgement call (standing, but full of radio gear and not in use as a lookout) and can be dropped. Staffing 'unstaffed as of 2023' rests on the 2023 year-end report and the 1990 last-staffed date. The 2024 and 2025 Cal-South annual reports (cr-cal-south-2024.pdf, cr-cal-south-2025.pdf) show the same repeater-gear wording in search snippets but were not read, because of the page budget. A 2025 report snippet (cr-cal-s-m-2025.pdf) says there is no current direction to move the repeater equipment out of the lookout; also unread. The FFLA Monterey page gives its location as '60 miles southeast of Monterey', which looks wrong, so it is not used. Historical cab and roof facts are from the register and Forest Lookouts page; the 1923 build year is consistent across both. No new photos. Budget used: 6 distinct pages and 2 web searches.
